claims.text: The target material is an equimolar CoFeMnNiCr high-entropy alloy treated as a refractory alloy.
TOR-TILD's EAM references have limited ability to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid.
The proposed reference potential will be trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations from both solid and liquid states near and above melting.
The training workflow will use active learning and validation against independent ab initio datasets.
Independent validation and active learning will ensure comprehensive configurational coverage.
Machine-learned interatomic potentials can map three-dimensional atomic configurations to configurational energies.
Machine-learning descriptors can numerically represent local chemical and structural atomic environments.
A flexible neural-network descriptor space will capture the full spectrum of many-body interactions in the high-entropy liquid.
Broader descriptor and configurational coverage will improve phase-space overlap between the reference potential and ab initio liquid.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will shorten or reduce mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
Reduced thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will reduce the resulting free-energy error relative to EAM-based integration.
The deep-learning reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration mismatch by a factor of 2–3 relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The resulting free-energy estimates will be within a few meV per atom of direct ab initio benchmarks.
Better treatment of liquid configurations will improve predictions of free-energy differences and possible phase transitions.
Machine-learning potentials can be used for molecular-dynamics melting calculations that are impractical or resource-intensive with direct ab initio simulation.
The proposed approach applies to equimolar refractory high-entropy alloys over approximately 0.9Tm to 1.1Tm.
Applicability to non-equimolar alloys or substantially lower-melting systems has not been established.
Deviation exceeding approximately 10 meV per atom from direct ab initio free energies, or unreliable integration-path convergence, will falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of the integration path to converge reliably indicates poor reference–target phase-space overlap.
